newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan merges state commodity trading bodies.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan merges state commodity trading bodies.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker government said on Wednesday it would merge three state-run commodity trading corporations to cut costs and improve efficiency.

A government statement said Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's cabinet had decided to merge the Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) and the Cotton Export Corporation (CEC) with the Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP).
"The decision to merge RECP and CEC into TCP was taken in pursuance of the government's policy of restructuring public sector corporations," the statement said.

It said RECP had virtually lost its role after the rice trade was privatised in 1990 and had "degenerated into a loss-making enterprise" whose losses had accumulated to 8.68 billion rupees by fiscal 1994/95 (July-June).

Similarly, the CEC had become redundant when the private sector was allowed to trade in cotton in 1987/88, turning it into a "dormant organisation, causing the national exchequer nearly 320 million rupees loss per annum without any benefit".
It said the TCP, which handles most of Pakistan's vegetable oil imports among other food commodities, had been retained because it was a commercially viable corporation.
